key_insight: Simulated neuronal damage produces architecture-dependent language failures: gradual decline in LSTMs, late collapse under Transformer MLP ablation, and smoother decline under attention-head ablation.
engineering_relevance: These failure profiles offer a computational analogy for progressive damage and functional reserve, rather than a validated solid-mechanics damage model.
method: Systematically ablate computational units in LSTM and Transformer language models.
Compare Transformer feedforward MLP and attention-head ablation.
Apply limited fine-tuning as a proxy for compensatory plasticity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parallel syntactic and semantic decline in LSTMs, versus distinct Transformer degradation curves and qualitative semantic errors resembling aspects of aphasia.
watch_item: Aphasia and neurodegeneration parallels are qualitative; computational ablation and limited fine-tuning do not establish biological equivalence.
paper_title: Can Language Models Get "Aphasia" From Neuronal Ablation?
